title: Tournaments and events
summary: TCG Card Shop Simulator gives events their own machinery: the game keeps tournament data for customers, and formats, screens and prices for the events you run.
body: Events are set up through dedicated screens rather than being an ordinary sale, which is why a format and a price are chosen separately.
Customer interest is tracked as its own data, so who takes part is something the game knows rather than something you count by eye.
Prizes have their own shelf, so what a winner receives is a display you place rather than a line in a ledger.
What this entry does not tell you: how often events run, what entry should cost or what prizes are worth. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Customer participation in tournaments is tracked as its own data.
An event is set up through its own screens.
The prize shelf is something a customer interacts with, and it carries a screen with materials of its own.
The event side ships fittings of its own: a statue podium with a dark and a dark shiny material, prize shelves with a screen mesh for them, and a group for attaching a customer's prize.
facts.evidence: asset names: StatuePodium, MAT_StatuePodium_Dark, MAT_StatuePodium_DarkShinny, TournamentPrizeShelf_Mesh, TournamentPrizeShelfScreen_Mesh, CustomerTournamentPrizeAttachGrp, Stop Pad Event
